prompt: A model spacecraft of total mass 1.80 kg is at rest in deep space. It fires its thruster, expelling 0.20 kg of exhaust gas at a speed of 360 m s^-1 relative to the spacecraft. What is the speed gained by the remaining spacecraft body?

answer.explanation: Mass of remaining spacecraft body = 1.80 kg - 0.20 kg = 1.60 kg. Total initial momentum is zero. Backward momentum of gas = 0.20 kg x 360 m s^-1 = 72 kg m s^-1. By conservation of momentum, forward momentum of spacecraft = 72 kg m s^-1. Speed = 72 / 1.60 = 45 m s^-1.

distractor_explanations: Correct: remaining mass is 1.60 kg, so speed gained = (0.20 x 360) / 1.60 = 72 / 1.60 = 45 m s^-1.
Dividing by the initial total mass 1.80 kg instead of remaining mass: 72 / 1.80 = 40 m s^-1.
Arbitrary estimate assuming speed is 10% of exhaust speed.
hints: What is the mass of the spacecraft body after expelling the gas?
Equate forward momentum of spacecraft to backward momentum of gas.
solution: Option 1 is correct. Remaining mass M = 1.80 - 0.20 = 1.60 kg. M v = m_gas v_gas => 1.60 v = 0.20 x 360 = 72 => v = 45 m s^-1.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 2: Calculate momentum carried by gas: 0.20 x 360 = 72 kg m s^-1.
Step 3: By conservation of momentum, M_remaining x v = 72.
